query_text: what is a good title for a poem I'm writing about a religious boy who has been sheltered from the outside world by his family, but one day he leaves his house and sees the reality of the world?

content.text:
Here are some title ideas for your poem, each capturing a different tone or angle of the story:

1. **"Beyond the Threshold"** – Representing the moment he steps past the boundary of his sheltered life.
2. **"First Light"** – Symbolizing his first real glimpse of the world outside his faith-bound home.
3. **"The Unveiled World"** – Suggesting the world being "uncovered" before his innocent eyes.
4. **"Outside Eden"** – A religious metaphor comparing his sheltered home to paradise, and the outside world to the fall.
5. **"Broken Stained Glass"** – Implying that his rose-colored, church-window view of the world has been shattered.
6. **"The Other Side of Prayer"** – Hinting that the reality he discovers exists beyond the walls of his faith.
7. **"Where God Doesn't Reach"** – A provocative title suggesting he finds places or situations that feel untouched by divinity.
8. **"Dust and Revelation"** – Blending the earthiness of the real world with the religious concept of divine revelation.
9. **"The Prodigal's First Step"** – A nod to the Biblical Prodigal Son, focusing on the moment of departure.
10. **"Uncharted Gospel"** – Suggesting he discovers a new, unwritten "truth" about the world beyond his upbringing.

My personal recommendation would be **"Outside Eden"** — it's concise, poetic, and immediately evokes both the religious background and the theme of lost innocence. Good luck with your poem! 🙏✍️
